study.title: Machine Learning in Neuroimaging: A New Approach to Understand Acupuncture for Neuroplasticity
study.study_design: Systematic narrative review of studies integrating machine learning and neuroimaging in acupuncture promoting neuroplasticity
study.population: Reviewed studies included healthy subjects, patients with migraine, patients with chronic low back pain, and patients with functional dyspepsia
study.disease_condition: Multiple (migraine, chronic low back pain, functional dyspepsia, healthy subjects) — review article covering multiple included studies

extraction_notes.note: This is a review article (not a primary study). All extracted data are summaries of 10 included studies as reported in the review's Table 1 and narrative text. Primary data, detailed statistical outputs, full coordinate tables, and preprocessing parameters were not provided in the review itself. Where original study data is referenced, it is accessible only through the cited primary papers (references 45–54).

The review states 'The details of data acquisition and literature selection process can be found in the supplementary materials (available here).' The supplementary materials were not provided in the PDF and could not be extracted.

Sensory/interoceptive responses (deqi, pain, needling sensations) are not reported for any of the 10 included studies within the review text or Table 1. No deqi measurement instruments or values are documented.
Expectancy, blinding success, credibility, and allocation guessing were not reported in this review for any included study.
Adverse events were not reported in this review for any included study.

Neuroimaging acquisition parameters (scanner model, field strength, TR, TE, voxel size, preprocessing pipeline) are not reported in this review article. These would need to be obtained from the individual primary studies.

Statistical thresholds and multiple comparison correction methods used by the included studies are not uniformly reported in this review. The review's Table 1 provides only high-level ML algorithm and validation information.
The coordinate space (MNI, Talairach, or other) used by the included studies is not reported in the review. No coordinates are provided in Table 1 or the review narrative.

For López et al. 2013: the review states the classifier 'performed better when the training data was extracted from the verum ACU group,' but exact accuracy values (ACC, SPE, SEN) for this comparison are not provided numerically in the review text.
For Xue et al. 2011: the review states 'the performance of the classifier was not mentioned in this study' — this was faithfully reproduced in the extraction.

The sham acupuncture procedures for López et al. 2013 and Tu et al. 2019 sham group are described only minimally in this review (no penetration depth, needle type, or device details). These details would need to be obtained from the primary publications.

For Li et al. 2010 (GB37 vs NAP): Table 1 lists sample sizes as '11/11, 21.4 ± 1.8; GB37: 11, /, /; NAP: 11, /, /' which is ambiguous — it appears the 11 subjects from GB37 and 11 from NAP may be the same 22 participants in a within-subject crossover, but this is not clearly stated.

For Hao et al. 2008 and Jung et al. 2019: the validation method column in Table 1 contains '/' indicating not reported/not applicable for validation or that validation details were not described in the review.

Several n_analyzed values for contrasts were inferred from the sample size information in Table 1 (e.g., total responder + nonresponder for Liu 2018 = 38 + 56 = 94). These are internal calculations based on reported group sizes, not independently stated in the contrast result rows.
The PMID for this article was not found in the PDF. The DOI 10.1155/2020/8871712 was explicitly stated in the PDF header.

The Liu et al. 2018 study used sham ACU at NAP as the intervention but classified patients as 'responders' and 'nonresponders' to sham/placebo treatment. Both arm entries (arm_Liu2018_responder and arm_Liu2018_nonresponder) are coded as sham_acupuncture as that was the intervention applied.
